block.prompt:
SPEAKING — your final word (about one minute, on your own).

After today's talks and the debate, give a short spoken statement to the class:
- What is YOUR position on a cashless society now?
- Did anything you heard today change or sharpen your view? Say what, and why.
- Finish with ONE clear reason for where you stand.

Jot down up to four points below to guide you — then speak; don't read.
block.answer_key: Open — this is a short, connected personal statement. A strong one states a clear position, refers to a SPECIFIC moment from the lesson that influenced it, and ends on one firm reason. Model: “At the start I thought going cashless was obviously the future. But the power-cut scenario and Mr/Mrs C's role changed my mind a bit: a fully cashless town shuts some people out and stops working the moment the system fails. So my position now is that we should go mostly digital but keep cash as a guaranteed backup — because a payment system that can exclude people or break down completely isn't really progress.” Assess whether the statement is coherent, personal and reasoned — not which side it lands on.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Jede Haltung ist zulässig. Bewertet werden Kohärenz des Kurzmonologs, der erkennbare Bezug auf einen konkreten Moment des Unterrichts (Lernnachweis) und eine klare Abschlussbegründung.

levels: Clear position, connected delivery, firm closing reason
Position and reason present but loosely connected
Fragmented; no clear stance or ending
Names a specific moment from the lesson that shaped the view
Refers to the lesson only in general terms
No reference to what was heard today

watch_outs: ‚Did anything change your view?' wird oft mit ‚no' abgetan — dann fehlt der Reflexionsteil. Ermutigen, wenigstens EINEN Moment (Szenario, Rolle, Gegenargument) konkret zu benennen.
Vom Zettel ablesen verhindert freies Sprechen — nur Stichworte, kein ausformulierter Text (daher nur vier Notizzeilen).
Auf einen sauberen Schluss achten (‚All things considered, …' / ‚On balance, …') statt eines Abbruchs mitten im Satz.

subject: Lebende Fremdsprache
kompetenzbereich: An Gesprächen teilnehmen und zusammenhängendes Sprechen
